exo.texte: The sun is shining in the blue sky. Birds are singing in the trees. Emma has a new bike. This morning, she decides to go for a ride. She puts on her helmet and goes out to the park. She rides slowly on the paths. The wind blows through her hair. Emma smiles; she loves her red bike.

In summer, the grasshopper was singing under the sun. When winter came, she had nothing left to eat. So she went to see the ant and asked for some food. But the ant, being prudent, told her that one must think of the future and work before it's too late.

Emma Bovary dreamed of great adventures and a life full of passion. However, she lived in a small village where every day was the same. Her husband, Charles, was a simple and caring man, but Emma wanted something else. She spent hours reading novels, hoping to find in them the escape she couldn't have in reality.

Julien Sorel was an ambitious and intelligent young man. Born into a modest family, he dreamed of climbing the social ladder. He spent hours reading books, learning Latin, and studying great historical figures. When he was hired as a tutor in a wealthy family, he saw it as an opportunity to change his destiny. But his quest for power and his passionate heart would soon clash with the cruel realities of his time.

exo.titre: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
exo.texte: The Nautilus moved silently through the deep waters. Through the submarine's huge windows, Professor Aronnax observed marine creatures he had never seen before. Luminous jellyfish floated gently, while schools of colorful fish passed by at high speed. Captain Nemo, mysterious and taciturn, stood by the helm, staring at the invisible horizon. Each day brought its share of discoveries, but also mysteries that troubled the crew.

Mowgli, the little boy raised by wolves, loved running through the jungle. His friends Baloo, the wise bear, and Bagheera, the black panther, taught him the laws of the jungle. Each day was a new adventure: he climbed trees, swam in rivers, and played with monkeys. But the jungle wasn't without danger. Shere Khan, the fierce tiger, always lurked in the shadows, seeking to attack the young boy.

exo.titre: Around the World in Eighty Days
exo.texte: Phileas Fogg was a very punctual man. Every morning, he followed the same routine: he got up at eight o'clock, had his tea, then read the newspaper. One day, he made a bet with his friends. He claimed he could travel around the world in just 80 days.

Last year, I visited a small town by the sea. The streets were paved and lined with colorful houses. Every morning, I had my coffee on a terrace overlooking the ocean. I also tasted delicious local dishes, like freshly caught seafood. But what struck me most were the sunsets, when the sky became a mix of pink, orange, and purple.

Luna, the little grey cat, was very curious. One day, she decided to explore the house's attic. She jumped onto an old chair, then onto a dusty shelf. There, she discovered a cardboard box full of old photographs. Fascinated, she started playing with one of the photos, making it fall to the ground. Luna loved her little adventures, even if it often meant getting scolded by her owners!

Oliver Twist was an orphan who grew up in miserable conditions. After daring to ask for 'more soup,' he was sent to work for an undertaker. But Oliver couldn't bear this life anymore. One day, he ran away to London, where he was taken in by a group of thieves led by the sinister Fagin. Despite the difficulties and dangers, Oliver always hoped to find a place where he could be happy and safe.

Heidi, a lively young girl, was sent to live with her grandfather in the Alps mountains. Although her grandfather was a rough and solitary man, Heidi learned to love him and admire the beauty of nature that surrounded her. She spent her days running in the meadows, playing with goats, and enjoying the fresh air. But one day, Heidi was sent to live in the city, far from her beloved mountains. She dreamed of returning home, where she felt truly happy.

After a shipwreck, Robinson Crusoe found himself alone on a desert island. At first, he was desperate. But quickly, he understood that he had to organize himself to survive. He built a cabin, hunted animals for food, and learned to cultivate the land. Days passed, then months, and finally years. Robinson wondered if he would ever see another human being again. One day, he spotted footprints in the sand, and his life changed forever.

exo.titre: Tales from the Thousand and One Nights
exo.texte: Scheherazade was a young woman gifted with great intelligence and a talent for storytelling. Each night, she captivated the king by narrating wonderful tales, full of magic and mysteries. She spoke of genies trapped in lamps, treasures hidden in caves, and journeys on flying carpets. Each morning, she would stop at the most exciting moment, forcing the king to wait for the continuation. Thus, she managed to postpone her execution night after night.

Edmond Dantès was a young and ambitious sailor, ready to marry the woman he loved. But jealous enemies plotted to send him to prison for a crime he didn't commit. Locked in the fortress of Château d'If, he lost all hope. However, an old prisoner revealed a secret to him: a treasure hidden on the island of Monte Cristo. After years of captivity, Edmond escaped and became a rich and powerful man, ready to take revenge on those who had betrayed him.

Jonathan Harker traveled to Transylvania to meet a mysterious client, Count Dracula. Upon arrival, he was struck by the strange and sinister atmosphere of the castle. Gradually, Jonathan discovered that Dracula was not just a man, but a terrifying creature who fed on human blood. Meanwhile, in London, disturbing events began to occur. Lucy, a friend of Jonathan's fiancée, fell seriously ill, and no one understood why. The battle against Dracula was just beginning.

The Paris Opera was a magical place where the greatest singers performed. But it was also haunted by a mysterious phantom. He lived in the basement and demanded that certain rules be respected. Christine, a young singer, caught the phantom's attention. He taught her the secrets of singing and encouraged her to become a great artist. However, his love for Christine became obsessive, and he was ready to do anything to keep her by his side, even if it meant spreading terror.

Buck, a powerful dog, lived peacefully in a large house in California. But one day, he was captured and sold to work as a sled dog in the Canadian north. There, he discovered a harsh and merciless world. Every day, he fought against the cold, hunger, and dangers of the wild forest. Gradually, Buck felt nature's call within him. He learned to survive, to fight, and to listen to his instincts, until he became the leader of the pack.

The sound of waves was soothing. Claire was walking on the beach, collecting seashells. 'Look at this one,' she said, showing a spiral shell to her son. He took it and exclaimed, 'It looks like treasure!' Claire smiled. 'Each shell has a story to tell.' As they continued their walk, they found a glass bottle containing a message. 'A message in a bottle? It's just like in stories!' said the boy. Claire carefully opened the bottle.

The storm was raging, and the boat was pitching violently. 'Everyone stay calm!' shouted the captain. The sailors held onto the rigging, their faces marked with fear. Suddenly, lightning illuminated the horizon, revealing an island. 'Land!' someone cried out. The captain adjusted his spyglass. 'Prepare to dock there,' he ordered. The boat moved forward with difficulty, but the crew kept hope. Upon reaching the beach, they discovered a dense and mysterious jungle, full of strange noises.

In the old abandoned station, silence reigned supreme. Luc moved forward cautiously, flashlight in hand. The walls were covered with colorful graffiti, and pieces of broken glass littered the floor. A broken clock still showed 3:42. 'What happened here?' he wondered. Suddenly, footsteps echoed behind him. He turned quickly, but there was no one there. Yet the feeling of being watched wouldn't leave him.

'Stop here, look at this incredible view!' exclaimed Clara, pointing at the horizon. Paul slowed the car and parked by the roadside. Before them, a verdant valley stretched as far as the eye could see. Birds flew low, tracing arcs in the clear sky. Clara took out a notebook and pencil. 'What are you doing?' asked Paul, intrigued. 'I want to draw this moment,' she replied with a smile. While she was sketching, Paul took a photo with his phone. 'A memory to share!' he said.

In the old house, Emile pushed open a door that had been closed for years. A musty smell filled the air. On a wooden table, he found a broken clock and a dusty journal. 'What does this old notebook say?' he whispered as he opened it. The yellowed pages were filled with handwritten notes and strange sketches. One phrase caught his attention: 'The key is under the living room carpet.' Emile ran to check. Under the carpet, he found a small metal box secured with a padlock. 'And now, where's the key to the padlock?'

'Come in,' said a hoarse voice behind the door. Lea hesitated but pushed the door and entered the small shop. Inside, shelves loaded with ancient objects creaked under their weight. A wall clock ticked irregularly. 'I'm looking for a unique gift,' said Lea. The old man behind the counter smiled: 'You're in the right place. Look at this.' He pulled out a ring inlaid with a strange purple crystal. 'It's perfect,' whispered Lea. As she reached for it, a shiver ran through her. Was it just a coincidence?

A bright glint caught Max's attention in the snowy field. He approached and found a silver medallion, engraved with a date: '12-07-1945.' 'Where did this come from?' he whispered. Opening it, he discovered an old photograph: a young couple smiling. Max showed the object to his grandmother. Her eyes welled up. 'It belonged to your grandfather. He lost it during the war.' Max clutched the medallion. 'I'll have it restored,' he said. His grandmother smiled weakly, grateful.

'Listen carefully,' said the professor, adjusting his glasses. 'This ancient text contains riddles.' The students leaned over the parchment, fascinated. The engraved words seemed to glow faintly. 'What does this strange symbol mean?' asked Mark. The professor explained: 'It represents eternity.' While he was speaking, Lucy noticed a detail: one letter was highlighted in each line. 'Look, it forms a word!' she said. The group deciphered the message: 'Follow the light.' Intrigued, they tried to figure out what it meant.

'Sir, you dropped this,' said the child, holding out a key adorned with a strange symbol. The man looked surprised: 'But... where did it come from?' The boy shrugged. 'I found it right there, at the foot of this tree.'

A walk in the forest at twilight reveals wonders often ignored. The rays of the setting sun pass through the trees, creating plays of shadow and light. The scent of damp earth fills the fresh air. The concert began in a packed hall. The first musical notes resonated, immediately captivating the audience. Each instrument seemed to tell a story, and the spectators were transported to another universe.

Children were playing in the park, laughing and chasing after a red balloon. The sky was brilliantly blue, and parents chatted on benches, watching over the little ones. The atmosphere was joyful, like a moment suspended in time.

The sign read: 'Warning, danger!' but no one seemed to pay attention to it. The rain was falling heavily, lightning tore through the sky, and the sound of drops crashing against the windows was hypnotically regular. Sitting by the lake, he listened to the soothing sounds of nature. The leaves of the trees rustled softly, and the water sparkled under the sun's rays. This simple moment brought him deep peace.
